finding: src/anomaly/owners.py:59 Phase attempts do not stage or atomically promote owner outputs.
rationale: The public dispatcher reaches this path with normal phase inputs, but deterministic and dynamic owners write against the live case root while the attempt utility records only a post-hoc result and has no validation, promotion, or rollback of owner artifacts, so a later owner failure can leave partially committed case state and the high-severity AC3 violation is reachable.

evidence.output: The installed operating contract requires every phase's outputs to be written under .anomaly/attempts/<phase>/attempt-<n>/ first, validated for hashes, schemas, safety, and relative paths, and only then moved into case folders; superseded attempts must remain auditable.

run_workflow passes both case_root and attempt_dir into consume_owner. Handler dispatch then calls _run_handler, whose attempt parameter is named _attempt_dir and unused while every deterministic operation receives root. Dynamic dispatch invokes the reasoning owner with only case_root, and P5 rejects the result unless live root/findings/draft.json already exists.

run_attempts calls execute(attempt_dir) before writing only result.json into the attempt directory. On exception it records failure.json and state evidence but performs no owner-output rollback; on success _seal_success only updates identities/state and performs no artifact validation or atomic promotion.

Reachable deterministic phases perform compound live mutations: P4 seals Gate A and then executes detectors, while detector execution creates live run directories, snapshots, provenance, and appends signals inside a per-detector loop before later operations can raise; P7 likewise accepts findings, writes the report, and only then generates charts. No phase-level transaction protects these sequences.
